```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.6, dpi = 90)
has_terra <- requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE)
has_sf <- requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE)
```

A burn is a lookup table. To ask whether a point is inside a polygon, find
the point's cell: if the cell is in a run the answer is yes, if it has no
record the answer is no, and only an edge cell needs the polygon itself.

`relate = TRUE` takes that idea from points to cells, and from "inside" to
every spatial predicate. For each polygon and each grid cell it gives the
**DE-9IM matrix**: nine entries saying how the polygon's interior, boundary
and exterior meet the cell's interior, boundary and exterior, each `F`
(empty) or the dimension `0`, `1` or `2` of the intersection. The crate
computes it after the burn, from the geometry, and only for the cells the
polygon's boundary touches. Every other cell is already answered by the burn.

## One polygon

The polygon from the crate's book has edges along cell walls and diagonals
through cell corners.

```{r one}
library(cbr)
ring <- rbind(c(1, 1), c(6, 1), c(6, 3), c(8.5, 5.5), c(4, 7), c(1, 4), c(1, 1))
g <- wk::wkt(sprintf("POLYGON ((%s))", paste(ring[, 1], ring[, 2], collapse = ", ")))
b <- cb_burn(g, extent = c(0, 10, 0, 8), dimension = c(10, 8), relate = TRUE)
b
head(b$relations)
```

The relations hold the cells the boundary touches: 43 here. Any cell's matrix
comes from `cb_matrix()`, which falls back on the burn for the rest: a cell in
a run is covered (`212FF1FF2`), any other is disjoint (`FF2FF1212`).

```{r lookup}
cells <- data.frame(row = c(5, 7, 8, 1, 1), col = c(4, 3, 3, 4, 10),
                    what = c("deep inside", "above the bottom edge", "below the bottom edge",
                             "at the top vertex", "far away"))
cells$matrix <- cb_matrix(b, cells$row, cells$col)
cells
```

The cell below the bottom edge shares a line with the polygon (boundary
against boundary is `1`) and no area. The one at the top vertex shares a
single point (`0`). Neither has a record in the burn: no part of them is
covered. They are exactly the cells an *all-touched* rasterization should
add, and the ones a burn's records cannot find.

`cb_cells_where()` selects cells by predicate:

```{r predicates}
sapply(c("intersects", "interiors_meet", "covers", "touches"),
       function(p) nrow(cb_cells_where(b, p)))
c(cells_with_a_record = sum(!is.na(cb_materialize(b, "count"))),
  cells_touched = sum(!is.na(cb_materialize(b, "intersects"))))
```

```{r one-figure, fig.height = 4.2}
draw_cells <- function(b, ring) {
  dm <- attr(b, "dimension")
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, dm[1]), ylim = c(0, dm[2]), asp = 1, axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  cell <- function(t, ...) rect(t$col - 1, dm[2] - t$row, t$col, dm[2] - t$row + 1, ...)
  covers <- cb_cells_where(b, "covers")
  part <- cb_cells_where(b, "interiors_meet")
  part <- part[!paste(part$row, part$col) %in% paste(covers$row, covers$col), ]
  cell(covers, col = "#f97316", border = "white")
  cell(part, col = "#fdba74", border = "white")
  cell(cb_cells_where(b, "touches"), col = "#e7e5e4", border = "white")
  abline(v = 0:dm[1], h = 0:dm[2], col = "grey85", lwd = 0.5)
  lines(ring, lwd = 2)
  legend("topright", inset = c(-0.02, 0), bty = "n", cex = 0.8, xpd = NA,
         fill = c("#f97316", "#fdba74", "#e7e5e4"),
         legend = c("covers", "shares part of its area", "touches only"))
}
par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 8))
draw_cells(b, ring)
```

## Exact all-touched, against GDAL

GDAL's rasterizer has an *all-touched* mode, which `terra::rasterize(touches
= TRUE)` uses: a cell is burned if the polygon's boundary passes through it.
It is a fast, widely used approximation. With the relations, cbr's
`cb_materialize(value = "intersects")` is the exact version: every cell whose
closed box shares at least a point with the polygon.

The difference shows where boundaries run along cell walls. Natural Earth
draws several borders on meridians and parallels: Egypt's with Libya on 25°E
and with Sudan on 22°N, and the United States' with Canada on 49°N. On a 1°
grid those borders lie exactly on cell walls.

```{r world}
ne <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "ne_110m_countries.rds", package = "cbr"))
countries <- ne$geometry
world <- cb_burn(countries, extent = c(-180, 180, -90, 90), dimension = c(360, 180), relate = TRUE)
world
touched <- cb_cells_where(world, "intersects")
touched$cell <- (touched$row - 1L) * 360L + touched$col
```

```{r terra, eval = has_terra}
r <- terra::rast(nrows = 180, ncols = 360, xmin = -180, xmax = 180, ymin = -90, ymax = 90,
                 crs = "OGC:CRS84")
v <- terra::vect(as.character(wk::as_wkt(countries)), crs = "OGC:CRS84")
gdal <- lapply(seq_along(v), function(k) {
  which(!is.na(terra::values(terra::rasterize(v[k], r, touches = TRUE), mat = FALSE)))
})
exact <- split(touched$cell, factor(touched$id, levels = seq_along(v)))
cmp <- data.frame(country = ne$name, cbr = lengths(exact), gdal = lengths(gdal),
                  only_cbr = mapply(function(a, b) length(setdiff(a, b)), exact, gdal),
                  only_gdal = mapply(function(a, b) length(setdiff(b, a)), exact, gdal))
colSums(cmp[-1])
cmp[cmp$only_cbr + cmp$only_gdal > 0, ]
```

The two agree on all but six countries, those with borders on cell walls.
cbr finds 82 cells GDAL misses, and GDAL has 4 cells cbr does not. Which is
right can be settled cell by cell with GEOS, relating each country to each
disputed cell's box:

```{r geos, eval = has_terra && has_sf}
old <- suppressMessages(sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE))
box <- function(cell) {
  row <- (cell - 1) %/% 360 + 1; col <- (cell - 1) %% 360 + 1
  x0 <- -180 + col - 1; y1 <- 90 - (row - 1)
  sf::st_sfc(sf::st_polygon(list(rbind(c(x0, y1 - 1), c(x0 + 1, y1 - 1), c(x0 + 1, y1),
                                       c(x0, y1), c(x0, y1 - 1)))))
}
geos <- function(id, cells) {
  p <- sf::st_as_sfc(wk::as_wkt(countries[id]))
  vapply(cells, function(cl) sf::st_relate(p, box(cl))[1, 1], "")
}
disputed <- do.call(rbind, lapply(which(cmp$only_cbr + cmp$only_gdal > 0), function(k) {
  only_cbr <- setdiff(exact[[k]], gdal[[k]])
  only_gdal <- setdiff(gdal[[k]], exact[[k]])
  data.frame(id = k, cell = c(only_cbr, only_gdal),
             found_by = rep(c("cbr only", "GDAL only"), c(length(only_cbr), length(only_gdal))))
}))
disputed$geos <- mapply(function(id, cl) geos(id, cl), disputed$id, disputed$cell)
disputed$cbr <- cb_matrix(world, (disputed$cell - 1) %/% 360 + 1, (disputed$cell - 1) %% 360 + 1, disputed$id)
with(disputed, table(found_by, geos_intersects = geos != "FF2FF1212"))
with(disputed, table(found_by, same_matrix_as_cbr = geos == cbr))
invisible(suppressMessages(sf::sf_use_s2(old)))
```

Every cell cbr adds does meet its country, nearly all along a wall or at a
corner, with exactly the matrix GEOS computes; the cells GDAL adds are a
fraction of a thousandth of a degree away from the country, burned by
rounding.

```{r border-figure, eval = has_terra, fig.height = 4}
outline <- function(id) {
  xy <- wk::wk_coords(countries[id])
  for (k in unique(paste(xy$part_id, xy$ring_id))) {
    s <- xy[paste(xy$part_id, xy$ring_id) == k, ]
    lines(s$x, s$y, lwd = 1.5)
  }
}
show <- function(id, xlim, ylim, title) {
  plot(NA, xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim, asp = 1, xlab = "", ylab = "", las = 1)
  draw <- function(cells, col) {
    row <- (cells - 1) %/% 360 + 1; col_ <- (cells - 1) %% 360 + 1
    rect(-180 + col_ - 1, 90 - row, -180 + col_, 90 - row + 1, col = col, border = "white")
  }
  draw(intersect(exact[[id]], gdal[[id]]), "#fdba74")
  draw(setdiff(exact[[id]], gdal[[id]]), "#c2410c")
  draw(setdiff(gdal[[id]], exact[[id]]), "#2563eb")
  outline(id)
  title(title, cex.main = 0.9)
}
egypt <- match("Egypt", ne$name); canada <- match("Canada", ne$name)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(2.5, 3, 2, 0.5))
show(egypt, c(22, 38), c(20, 33), "Egypt: borders on 25E and 22N")
show(canada, c(-112, -94), c(44, 56), "Canada: the 49N border")
legend("bottomleft", bty = "n", cex = 0.75, fill = c("#fdba74", "#c2410c", "#2563eb"),
       legend = c("both", "cbr only (touching)", "GDAL only"))
```

## Slivers the burn rounds away

The burn treats a coverage within 1e-6 of 0 or 1 as exactly 0 or 1, as the
crate's C++ ancestor and exactextract do. That is right for area: the error
is at most a millionth of a cell. But it means a cell holding a sliver of a
country can have no record, and a cell holding a sliver of a country's
exterior can be in a run. The relations come from the geometry, not the
records, so `cb_slivers()` can list those cells:

```{r slivers}
s <- cb_slivers(world)
s$country <- ne$name[s$id]
s$lon <- -180 + s$col - 0.5
s$lat <- 90 - s$row + 0.5
table(s$kind)
s[, c("country", "lon", "lat", "kind", "matrix")]
```

An `interior` sliver is a cell that shares area with the country although
the burn has no record there; an `exterior` sliver is a run cell that the
country does not in fact cover.

The relation of a polygon to a cell is only defined for valid polygons, and
the crate assumes them. Two countries in this dataset are not valid, so it is
worth checking before reading the table:

```{r validity, eval = has_sf}
old <- suppressMessages(sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE))
polys <- sf::st_as_sfc(wk::as_wkt(countries))
valid <- sf::st_is_valid(polys)
data.frame(country = ne$name[!valid], problem = sf::st_is_valid(polys[!valid], reason = TRUE))
```

How far off the burn's record is in each cell, from sf's area of the country
inside the cell:

```{r sliver-areas, eval = has_sf}
s$valid <- valid[s$id]
s$area_share <- mapply(function(id, row, col) {
  cell <- sf::st_sfc(sf::st_polygon(list(rbind(c(-180 + col - 1, 90 - row), c(-180 + col, 90 - row),
                                                c(-180 + col, 91 - row), c(-180 + col - 1, 91 - row),
                                                c(-180 + col - 1, 90 - row)))))
  hit <- sf::st_intersection(polys[id], cell)
  if (length(hit)) sum(as.numeric(sf::st_area(hit))) / as.numeric(sf::st_area(cell)) else 0
}, s$id, s$row, s$col)
s$off_by <- ifelse(s$kind == "interior", s$area_share, 1 - s$area_share)
s[, c("country", "lon", "lat", "kind", "valid", "off_by")]
invisible(suppressMessages(sf::sf_use_s2(old)))
```

Seventeen of the eighteen are genuine: the burn's record is off by less than
a millionth of a cell, within its tolerance, and the relation sees the
sliver. The exception is Sudan's cell at 33.5°E, 8.5°N. Sudan's ring crosses
itself just north of it, at 33.96°E, 9.46°N, and for a self-crossing ring
"inside" has no single meaning: the burn fills by winding and counts the cell
as covered, while GEOS's repaired polygon covers only a hundred-millionth of
it. That row is not a sliver but invalid input, which `sf::st_make_valid()`
(or a cleaner source) should fix before burning. (The United States is also
invalid, but where Alaska meets the Yukon, away from its sliver cells.)

None of this changes an area: the coverage fractions are what they should be
to a millionth of a cell. It changes topology, and for a question like "which
countries touch this cell", topology is the answer.
